meta.description: Frames Bayesian phylogenetics as a posterior over trees conditioned on data and priors, approximated by an MCMC that must be proven converged (ESS, PSRF, ASDSF), with MrBayes, BEAST2, RevBayes and PhyloBayes-MPI; covers branch-length priors, stepping-stone model comparison and CAT-GTR.
meta.executed: 6/7 inputs executed (MrBayes 3.2.7a Windows serial build, IQ-TREE 2.4.0 + AliSim, rwty 1.0.3 / R, Python 3.12 with numpy/pandas/DendroPy 5.0.13); Input 6 is a routing answer with no code
meta.execution_note: All alignments are SYNTHETIC (IQ-TREE AliSim from known trees, data/make_data.py): 12 taxa x 1500 bp GTR+G, an 8-taxon near-polytomy (central edge 0.0005), and 60 taxa x 800 bp with very short branches. MCMC lengths were cut to 20k-300k generations; seeds were added by the auditor because the Skill's MrBayes block sets none. The Skill's MrBayes block was also run VERBATIM (ngen=10000000) and halted itself at generation 5000. PhyloBayes-MPI has no Windows build: its flags were checked against the PhyloBayes-MPI 1.9 manual and NOT executed. BEAST2 and RevBayes were not installed; the Skill gives no runnable code for them.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated numbers or citations. Every ESS, PSRF, ASDSF, posterior probability, marginal likelihood and tree length reported came from MrBayes/IQ-TREE/rwty runs on the synthetic data. The key historical claim (gammadir default since 3.2.3) was verified in the 3.2.7a help and the v3.2.3 release notes.

practice_boundaries.detail: Pure research phylogenetics; nothing diagnoses, prescribes or triages an individual.

methodological_ground.detail: The agent never shipped an unconverged posterior: the early-halted stoprule runs (Inputs 1, 3) and the under-run chain (Input 2) were rejected on ESS, ASDSF and max split SD. Harmonic-mean model choice was refused (Input 7) and dating was not faked from substitution branch lengths (Input 6).

code_usability.detail: Every MrBayes command in the Skill (lset, prset gammadir, mcmc with stoprule/stopval/diagnfreq, sump/sumt burninfrac relburnin, ss nsteps) is accepted by 3.2.7a and exits 0. examples/bayesian_convergence.py passes py_compile and runs on real MrBayes .p files. The stoprule block is runnable but halts too early to be usable (P1), which is a correctness defect rather than unrunnable code. PhyloBayes flags match the manual (not executed).

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 3: MrBayes, stepping-stone and PhyloBayes are covered with commands; BEAST2 and RevBayes are named only, and the recommended prior-only check has no command (mcmc data=no). Correctness 3: the gammadir default history, flags and thresholds are verified. But the headline block's 'stoprule=yes stopval=0.01' with diagnfreq=5000 halts at generation 5000 on easy data, and the RWTY call 'burnin=25' is 25 trees in rwty 1.0.3, not 25%. Appropriateness 4.

reliability.note: The post-run convergence checklist and Common Errors table catch non-convergence, so fault tolerance is good. Error reporting is table-based. Recoverability 2: no guidance on checkpoints or 'mcmc append=yes' for extending a run, and the stoprule behaviour is undocumented.

performance_context.note: 235-line SKILL.md with dense tables and one 143-line example; loaded at once but compact.

agent_usability.note: Learnability 4. Consistency 3 (burninfrac=0.25 next to rwty burnin=25). Feedback design 3: an explicit convergence checklist but no reporting template. Error prevention 3: it does not warn that stoprule can halt before scalars are sampled, or that MrBayes sump itself prints 'Use the harmonic mean for Bayes factor comparisons of models'.

human_usability.note: The usage guide has natural example prompts. The description is long and jargon-dense (ASDSF, PSRF, CAT-GTR).

security.note: No credentials, network calls or eval. The example parses user files without validating the header (it raises NameError if no 'Gen' line).

maintainability.note: Clear sections and one self-testing example script. The self-test deliberately shows a PSRF FAIL, but no expected output is documented, and there is no test NEXUS for the MrBayes block.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger with explicit routing to modern-tree-inference, divergence-dating, species-trees and tree-io; strong escape hatches. Idempotency 2: the MrBayes block sets no seed/swapseed, so reruns differ.

key_strengths: Convergence doctrine is correct and operational: scalar vs topology diagnostics, ESS for every parameter, and >= 2 runs. It led the agent to reject every unconverged sample on the real MrBayes output
Factual claims verified on the binary: gammadir has been the default since 3.2.3 (3.2.7a help, v3.2.3 release notes), and all MrBayes flags are accepted
The harmonic-mean prohibition and stepping-stone recipe produced a correct Kass-Raftery Bayes factor, and the HME bias was reproduced (~65 log units)
The shipped convergence script runs on real MrBayes .p files and its verdicts agree with MrBayes sump
Clean routing to divergence-dating, modern-tree-inference, species-trees and tree-io; PhyloBayes bpcomp/tracecomp syntax and thresholds match the manual

recommendations.title: stoprule block halts before the chain is sampled
recommendations.problem: With 'stoprule=yes stopval=0.01 diagnfreq=5000' MrBayes stopped at gen 5000 (d12) and 20000 (star8) with minESS 2.7-34. Raising diagnfreq to 100000 still stopped with pinvar ESS 42.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill presents ASDSF auto-halt as the convergence gate. ASDSF can hit 0 on easy topologies long before scalars mix, and stoprule checks only topology.
recommendations.fix: Default to stoprule=no with an ngen sized for ESS > 200. If stoprule is kept, state that it is a topology-only minimum: add 'minpartfreq', a large diagnfreq, and a mandatory rerun/append ('mcmc append=yes ngen=...') until sump ESS > 200.

recommendations.title: Assertion pass rate below the Limited Release floor
recommendations.problem: 7 of 34 assertions failed (79.4%). They come from gaps in the Skill: stoprule, RWTY burnin, polytomy prior, SS per-step samples, prior-only command, and the MrBayes HME banner.
recommendations.root_cause: Several recommendations are stated as doctrine without a runnable command or a version-checked parameter.
recommendations.fix: Add runnable one-liners for each piece of advice (prior-only 'mcmc data=no', 'mcmc append=yes', ss samplefreq/alpha, rwty burnin in trees) and fix the items below.

recommendations.title: RWTY burnin=25 is trees, not percent
recommendations.problem: analyze.rwty(..., burnin=25) next to burninfrac=0.25 implies 25%, but rwty 1.0.3 documents burnin as a number of trees.
recommendations.root_cause: The parameter unit was not checked against ?analyze.rwty.
recommendations.fix: Write burnin = round(0.25 * length(run1$trees)) and note the unit.

recommendations.title: Warn that MrBayes sump recommends the harmonic mean
recommendations.problem: MrBayes 3.2.7a sump prints '(Use the harmonic mean for Bayes factor comparisons of models)', which contradicts the Skill.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill does not anticipate program output that invites the error it forbids.
recommendations.fix: Add a Common Errors row: ignore the sump HME banner and use ss / .ss marginal likelihoods.

recommendations.title: Seeds, SS per-step sampling and polytomy-prior tooling
recommendations.problem: The MrBayes block sets no seed/swapseed. The ss snippet gives no guidance on samples per step, alpha or burninss. The polytomy prior (Lewis 2005) has no command in any named tool, and prior-only sampling has no command.
recommendations.root_cause: The recipes stop at the headline command.
recommendations.fix: Add 'set seed= swapseed=', state '>= 30-50 samples per step (ngen/samplefreq/(nsteps+1))', name 'mcmc data=no' for prior-only runs, and state that the reversible-jump polytomy prior is not in MrBayes 3.2.7.
